content:
Nadia Brennan-Aziz
Senior Platform Engineer | Platform Engineering | Site Reliability Engineering

Email: [EMAIL] | Phone: [PHONE] | LinkedIn: [LINKEDIN] | GitHub: [GITHUB]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior Platform Engineer and platform team tech lead with experience building and operating AWS infrastructure and Kubernetes platforms. Strong hands-on experience with Terraform, EKS, infrastructure as code, service reliability, observability and capacity planning. Delivered an internal developer platform adopted by 14 product teams, reducing time from new service to production from approximately two weeks to under one day. Experienced in leading technical work across platform and product teams and communicating reliability goals with product leadership.

CORE SKILLS
Cloud and infrastructure: AWS, EKS, ECS, Terraform, Crossplane, infrastructure as code
Kubernetes and platform engineering: Kubernetes, Helm, Argo CD, Karpenter, golden-path service templates, Backstage catalog
Reliability and observability: SLOs, burn-rate alerting, Prometheus, Alertmanager, Grafana, Sloth, PagerDuty
Automation and development: Go, Python, GitHub Actions, controller-runtime
Performance and capacity: k6 load testing, capacity planning, AWS Spot

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd | 2022–Present
Tech lead of the platform team, responsible for the EKS platform, internal developer platform, SLOs and infrastructure cost initiatives.
- Built an internal developer platform with Go and Python service templates, Argo CD ApplicationSets and Crossplane compositions for RDS, SQS and S3 resources requested through pull requests.
- Reduced the time to take a new service to production from approximately two weeks to under one day; the platform was adopted by all 14 product teams.
- Replaced cluster-autoscaler managed node groups with Karpenter and introduced Spot capacity for stateless workloads with interruption handling, reducing EC2 spend by 38% (approximately £410,000 per year).
- Established SLOs and burn-rate alerts for the 20 most critical services using Prometheus recording rules and Sloth; reduced pages per week by approximately 60% and agreed an error-budget policy with product leadership.
- Work with platform and product teams to develop and operate reliable, observable services and infrastructure.

Site Reliability Engineer | Brightwater Games | 2019–2022
- Built and operated AWS infrastructure using Terraform and supported game backend reliability through launches with more than one million daily players.
- Replaced Nagios alerting with Prometheus and Alertmanager.
- Led capacity planning for two major launches.
- Used k6 to simulate 300,000 concurrent players ahead of a 2020 launch, identifying and resolving a connection-pool limit before launch.
- Operated EKS in production from 2020.

SELECTED PROJECTS

Kubernetes Preview Namespace Cleanup Operator | Open-source side project | 2024
- Built a small Kubernetes controller in Go using controller-runtime to delete expired preview namespaces.
- Project has approximately 120 GitHub stars.

SPEAKING AND MENTORING
- Speaker, UK DevOps meetup (2024): “SLOs that product managers care about”.
- Mentored three engineers moving from backend engineering into SRE.

CERTIFICATION
- Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA)

TECHNOLOGY
AWS, EKS, ECS, Terraform, Crossplane, Kubernetes, Karpenter, Argo CD, Helm, GitHub Actions, Prometheus, Alertmanager, Grafana, Sloth, PagerDuty, k6, Go, Python, controller-runtime, Backstage (catalog).

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured technical CV with clear progression from Site Reliability Engineer to Senior Platform Engineer and tech lead. The summary is focused, the skills are grouped logically, and the experience bullets use credible metrics: 14 product teams, production lead time reduced to under one day, 38% EC2 cost reduction, £410,000 annual savings, and 60% fewer pages. The document is professional and concise. Its main weakness is that it is optimized for platform engineering rather than this specific cloud infrastructure and fleet-connectivity role: networking, security, certificate management, and system-design terminology are not represented. There is no evident unsupported experience or skill in the document when compared with the supplied candidate information.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly parseable: it uses standard headings, plain text, conventional chronology, and no problematic tables, graphics, columns, or formatting. It contains strong ATS keywords for AWS, Terraform, Kubernetes, EKS, infrastructure as code, observability, reliability, SLOs, Go, Python, and capacity planning. AI screening probability is moderate to high for the AWS/platform/SRE aspects of the role, but materially lower for exact-match requirements such as Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, network design, practical security, and fleet or remote-device connectivity. Terraform is present, but Terragrunt is not supported by the candidate information and should not be added. The duplicated technology list is acceptable for ATS purposes, although it could be slightly streamlined.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with hands-on infrastructure engineering, AWS cloud operation, Terraform, reliability, observability, capacity planning, technical leadership, stakeholder engagement, and clear communication. The internal developer platform and production-operation experience also support the role's emphasis on helping backend developers deploy services that are easy to monitor and run. AWS is clearly shown, satisfying the relevant nice-to-have. The candidate's work leading the platform team and agreeing an error-budget policy with product leadership is particularly relevant to leading technical topics and bringing stakeholders along. Gaps in the candidate material are strong Terragrunt experience, networking knowledge specifically involving mTLS and SSL/TLS, certificate management, practical security work, IoT/automotive/remote-device integration, JVM experience, and explicit Linux or virtual-machine experience. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than defects that can be repaired through wording. The CV does show backend-adjacent work through game-backend reliability and Go/Python service templates, but not a clear JVM or full-stack background.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL/MEANINGFUL ALIGNMENT IMPROVEMENTS
1. In the Professional Summary section, revise the second sentence to foreground the job's supported infrastructure and stakeholder requirements. For example: "Strong hands-on experience designing, building and operating AWS infrastructure and Kubernetes platforms, with Terraform, infrastructure as code, service reliability, observability and capacity planning." Keep the existing metrics and do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, or security claims, because they are not supported by the candidate information.
2. In the Senior Platform Engineer section under Tallybrook Ltd, change the opening responsibility bullet from "Tech lead of the platform team, responsible for the EKS platform, internal developer platform, SLOs and infrastructure cost initiatives." to "Tech lead of the platform team, leading technical work across the EKS platform, internal developer platform, SLOs and infrastructure cost initiatives." This uses the job's leadership language while remaining supported and avoids implying people management.
3. In the Senior Platform Engineer section under Tallybrook Ltd, revise the internal developer platform bullet to make the system-design and backend-enablement relevance clearer: "Designed and built an internal developer platform with Go and Python service templates, Argo CD ApplicationSets and Crossplane compositions for RDS, SQS and S3 resources requested through pull requests, giving product teams a repeatable path to deploy services." This is a clarification of existing evidence, not an addition of unsupported experience.
4. In the Site Reliability Engineer section under Brightwater Games, revise the first bullet to make cloud infrastructure design and operation more explicit: "Designed, built and operated AWS infrastructure with Terraform, supporting game-backend reliability through launches with more than one million daily players." Only use "designed" if the candidate confirms that this accurately reflects the work; otherwise retain "Built and operated." 
5. In the Site Reliability Engineer section under Brightwater Games, combine the launch and load-testing bullets so the analytical contribution is easier for screening systems to identify: "Led capacity planning for two major launches; used k6 to simulate 300,000 concurrent players ahead of a 2020 launch, identifying and resolving a connection-pool limit before launch." 
6. In the Core Skills section, rename "Cloud and infrastructure" to "Cloud Infrastructure and Infrastructure as Code" and rename "Performance and capacity" to "Performance, Capacity Planning and Cost Optimization." This better mirrors the job description while retaining only supported skills.
7. In the Professional Experience section, replace the vague final Tallybrook bullet, "Work with platform and product teams to develop and operate reliable, observable services and infrastructure," with "Partner with platform and product teams to develop and operate reliable, observable services and infrastructure, and agree reliability goals with product leadership." This is supported by the existing error-budget-policy evidence and more directly addresses stakeholder engagement.
8. In the Technology section, retain AWS, Terraform, EKS, ECS, Kubernetes, observability tools, Go and Python, but remove the duplicate standalone technology list if space is limited after the revisions. The categorized Core Skills section already contains the same ATS terms; do not use the freed space to add unsupported terms such as Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, Linux or virtual machines.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, focused technical CV with clear progression from Site Reliability Engineer to Senior Platform Engineer and tech lead. The strongest content is quantified and outcome-oriented: platform adoption by 14 teams, production lead-time reduction, £410,000 annual cost reduction, 60% fewer pages, and capacity testing for 300,000 concurrent players. The document is professional, concise, and appropriately emphasizes AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform, reliability, observability, and technical leadership. The main content limitation is that the role-specific evidence is concentrated around platform engineering and SRE; the CV does not demonstrate the networking, certificate-management, or practical security aspects central to the fleet-connectivity role. Those are candidate-experience gaps rather than writing defects.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: it uses conventional section headings, plain text, readable chronology, standard job titles, and a strong concentration of relevant keywords such as AWS, Terraform, EKS, Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, observability, SLOs, Prometheus, and capacity planning. It should have a high ATS/AI screening probability for AWS platform, DevOps, and SRE roles. Screening probability for this specific vacancy is lower because the document contains no truthful evidence or keywords for Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, network design, or security. Do not insert those terms without supporting experience. The separate TECHNOLOGY section is somewhat repetitive because most technologies already appear in CORE SKILLS and EXPERIENCE, but it remains parseable and is not a major defect.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns strongly with the hands-on infrastructure, AWS, cloud operation, platform reliability, technical leadership, stakeholder engagement, analytical thinking, and communication aspects of the role. It also fits Corvale's engineering-led and ownership-oriented culture: the candidate has led platform work, built paved paths for product teams, operated systems end to end, and agreed reliability policy with product leadership. The CV demonstrates relevant backend-adjacent experience through Go, Python, service templates, and operating game backends. The candidate's material does not show Terragrunt, mTLS or SSL/TLS, certificate management, network design, practical security work, IoT/automotive/remote-device integration, JVM experience, Linux, or virtual-machine experience. These are genuine gaps and should not be represented as present through wording changes. AWS is clearly shown, and systems-design capability is reasonably evidenced through the internal developer platform, Crossplane compositions, service templates, and production infrastructure work, although the CV could label that connection more explicitly.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, revise the first sentence to make the design-and-operation match more explicit without adding unsupported experience. For example, change "Senior Platform Engineer and platform team tech lead with experience building and operating AWS infrastructure and Kubernetes platforms" to "Senior Platform Engineer and platform team tech lead with experience designing, building, and operating AWS infrastructure, Kubernetes platforms, and internal developer platforms." This is supported by the Tallybrook platform and infrastructure work.
2. In the Senior Platform Engineer section under Tallybrook Ltd, strengthen the stakeholder-leadership wording in the final bullet. Change "Work with platform and product teams to develop and operate reliable, observable services and infrastructure" to "Partner with platform and product teams to design, develop, and operate reliable, observable services and infrastructure, aligning technical work with product needs." This more directly reflects the job ad's language while remaining supported by the existing experience.
3. In the Site Reliability Engineer section under Brightwater Games, add the supported Atlantis detail to the Terraform bullet. Change "Built and operated AWS infrastructure using Terraform and supported game backend reliability through launches with more than one million daily players" to "Moved AWS infrastructure into Terraform with Atlantis and operated game backend infrastructure through launches with more than one million daily players." This improves specificity and uses evidence in the Original Candidate Information.
4. In the Tallybrook experience section, make the systems-design nature of the internal platform work clearer by revising the first bullet to begin "Designed and built an internal developer platform..." rather than only "Built an internal developer platform..." The existing service templates, Argo CD ApplicationSets, Crossplane compositions, and production-resource provisioning support this wording.
5. If retaining the separate TECHNOLOGY section, remove the duplicate technologies already fully covered in CORE SKILLS and keep it as a compact ATS keyword line; alternatively, retain it but ensure its spelling and capitalization exactly match the relevant experience bullets. This is optional and only a minor concision improvement.
